script.title: Audit Report vs Audit Certificate
script.caption_hook: Audit report or audit certificate: opinion or fact?

lines.say: Ma'am, audit report and audit certificate: are they the same thing?
Not quite. A report gives the auditor's opinion. A certificate confirms that a fact is correct.
So a report guarantees the accounts are fully correct?
No guarantee. A report is an opinion on true and fair view. A certificate states a fact.
Okay, and what does each one cover?
A report covers the whole financial statements. A certificate covers one item, like turnover.
Does the auditor check everything for both?
For a report, he uses test checks and sampling. For a certificate, he checks that item fully.
Can a certificate be qualified like a report?
No. A certificate is positive only. If he can't confirm the fact, he won't certify. A report can be qualified.
So he carries more responsibility for a certificate?
Yes, he vouches for the fact. Example: SA 700 audit report, or a net worth certificate.
Got it! Report is a reporter's view, certificate is a marksheet!
Exactly. Remember: report is opinion, certificate is fact.

check_notes: Writer: Fixed right_on words so each appears in its spoken line (certificate, item, positive). Versus right cards use the title "Fact" because "Certificate" exceeds 10 characters.

Checker: Lines 4, 6 and 10 (board, versus): the left column is labelled 'Report' but the right column is labelled 'Fact' instead of 'Certificate', so the board compares a document with a concept. Label the right column 'Certificate' (for example, lines 'States a fact' / 'Is correct').

Checker: Line 10 (voice): 'A certificate is positive only' is the traditional textbook distinction and fits the exam. But the ICAI Guidance Note on Reports or Certificates for Special Purposes (Revised 2016) does allow modified conclusions in certificates. A safer wording is: 'Traditionally, a certificate is not qualified. If he can't confirm the fact, he doesn't certify it.'
Checker: Line 13 (voice): the 'reporter's view' / 'marksheet' analogy is loose. A safer wording is 'report = expert opinion, certificate = confirmed fact'.
